title: clean.bats' marker pin is satisfied by comments, and clean's own walk markers are unpinned
body:
## Problem

clean.bats:1894 pins clean's marker test by running `grep -q -- "$marker"` over the whole of lib/helpers -- an unanchored regex, comments included -- and comment lines alone satisfy three of its four markers: CACHEDIR.TAG (four comment lines), `.rustc_info.json` (nine) and `debug/.fingerprint` (two). Only `release/.fingerprint` appears in code alone. And since 0148 moved the marker test, nothing pins clean's own walk markers (lib/cmd/clean:321, :325, :341). Parked at the 0.1.8 cut; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (cc's evidence pass)

Deleting the code for each of the first three markers leaves the arm green.

## Fix

The arm reads code only: `grep -F`, per function, over `declare -f _clean_marked_without_read _clean_has_markers _clean_peer_dirs`, which prints each function without its comments, and the same for `_clean_roots`. Measured: green on the base, red on each of the four mutants.

## Done when

1. Each of the four markers' code, deleted, turns the arm red; red at 2ce9411 for three of them.
2. clean's walk markers are pinned the same way.

## Resolution

Fixed at f3e1504b. The arm reads code only. `declare -f` prints a function without its comments, and each marker's whole test, such as `[ -f "$1/.rustc_info.json" ]`, is looked for with `grep -F` in the function that tests it, so a half-deleted test, its `-f` gone and the link test left, goes red too (critic-shell on 0170 v1, which pinned the bare names):
- `CACHEDIR.TAG` in `_clean_has_markers`;
- `.rustc_info.json`, `debug/.fingerprint` and `release/.fingerprint` in `_clean_marked_without_read`;
- `.rustc_info.json` in `cargo_target_root`, the per-node test 0168 made one.

clean's own walk markers, unpinned since 0148 moved the classifier, are pinned the same way in `_clean_roots`: `-name CACHEDIR.TAG`, `-name .rustc_info.json`, and the two `case` arms. lib/cmd/clean is sourced over a stub gatecmd whose `run_builtin_gate` runs nothing, so reading it runs no gate.

Driven with eight mutants, each deleting one marker's code, against the old arm and the new, and a ninth deleting half of `.rustc_info.json`'s test, against the new:
- The old arm stayed green for the tag, `.rustc_info.json` and `debug/.fingerprint`, the three the issue measured, and went red only for `release/.fingerprint`.
- It stayed green for all four of the walk's and the per-node test's mutants.
- The new arm goes red on all nine.

The function body is read up to the first line that is exactly `}`, which `declare -f` gives only the function's own close. A heredoc in the body holding such a line would end the read early, and a marker after it would read as absent: red, never green. The docstring says so.

The full suite on the landing tree: vc's full suite, on main af758c10 (code at 415ce738) with 0163 v3.1 and 0167 git-am'd, cc's 0155, 0160, 0161 and 0162 applied above them, and 0168, 0165, 0170 and 0171 applied above those, in a fresh clone: 2203 of 2203 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261006-0621), 06:21:47Z to 07:07:05Z; 5 skipped, the expected five: two arms that need a runner with no controlling terminal, two require_command arms whose expected outcome is a skip, and a case-folding disk.
